I wrote the solution to **`~/SOLUTION.md`**. Note: this environment has no `<project>/<project>-core` checkout (and the `gitreins` symlink is dangling), so the diagnosis is built from the supplied evidence + the documented procedure rather than a live re-run; the commands are written to be directly executable against the real repo.

## Solution summary

**Title:** Tier 1 "safety trigger" full-suite refusal caused by an inherited SHIM E2E failure

**Root cause (two facts):**
1. The guard escalated to **full-suite mode** (`test mode: diff, full suite — safety trigger`), so its verdict depended on an integration test the diff never touches.
2. That test (`tests/integration/test_consensus_e2e.py::TestSessionLifecycle::test_send_message_and_get_response`) is a **live-service HTTP test** that fails with `504 RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` whenever the sidecar can't answer in time — and it fails **identically at parent `e0c2310`** (1 failed in 90.55s). The diff only touches `pyproject.toml`, `src/main.py`, `src/quotas.py`, `src/security.py`, `tests/test_typing_gate.py`.

So the refusal is inherited, not diff-caused. Correct path: **attribution first, then a per-commit disclosed bypass.**

**Exact fix (key commands):**
1. Re-run the single id once to rule out a transient flake.
2. Prove inheritance in a scratch worktree at `e0c2310`, symlinking the venv:
   ```bash
   git worktree add -q --detach /tmp/pre-<tick> e0c2310
   cd /tmp/pre-<tick> && ln -s <main>/.venv .venv
   .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider "<failing::test>"
   ```
3. Compare: identical failure ⇒ inherited; different ⇒ fix the code.
4. Run diff-relevant gates by hand (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `tests/test_typing_gate.py`).
5. Commit with `--no-verify` **and** a body disclosing the test id, parent SHA + worktree result, clean lanes (secrets/lint), and hand-run gates — manually appending the required `Co-authored-by` trailer since `--no-verify` skips `prepare-commit-msg`.
6. Remove the worktree, then run the **tier-2 judge**.

**Verification:** tier-2 judge `3690aacb` independently ran the suite on the same tree and reported **`1422 passed, 1 skipped`**, proving the single guard failure was environmental/inherited. Final verdict: **Tier 1 PASS (degraded) + Tier 2 PASS**.

The document also lists the pitfalls explicitly: never `--no-verify` on first refusal, never a repo-wide hook disable, never a skip marker as the "fix", don't trust the test name over the guard header, don't skip the flake re-run, and don't forget the co-author trailer.

signatures.description:
SYMPTOM
A code commit with only local-source changes is REFUSED by the repository's commit-time
guard (gitreins Tier 1) with:

  Tier 1 Guards: FAIL  (test mode: diff, full suite — safety trigger)
    OK secrets - clean
    OK lint - ok
    X tests (full) - FAIL (tests/integration/test_consensus_e2e.py::TestSessionLifecycle::test_send_message_and_get_response [first failing id]; 1 failure(s))

The failing test is a LIVE-SERVICE integration test (it drives a running sidecar over
HTTP), so it fails whenever the backend cannot produce an agent response (504
RESPONSE_TIMEOUT). The guard fired its FULL-SUITE mode ("safety trigger") instead of the
usual diff-scoped mode, so a documented pre-existing integration failure blocks every
commit.

ROOT CAUSE / ATTRIBUTION
The failure is INHERITED, not caused by the staged diff. Two facts establish it:
1. The failing path (tests/integration/... live sidecar HTTP) is not touched by the diff
   (annotations + linter config + one new self-contained unit test).
2. The same test fails identically at the PRE-CHANGE commit in a clean detached worktree.
The repository documents this baseline in AGENTS.md "Known Issues": a full integration run
is expected to show pre-existing SHIM E2E failures.

FIX / PROCEDURE (attribution first, then a disclosed bypass)
a) Do NOT reach for --no-verify on the first refusal. Reproduce the failing id in a
   scratch worktree pinned to the pre-change commit and compare output + duration:

     git worktree add -q --detach /tmp/pre-<tick> <pre-change-sha>
     cd /tmp/pre-<tick>
     ln -s <main>/.venv .venv            # reuse the venv instead of reinstalling
     /path/to/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider "<failing::test>"

   Identical failure (same status code, same elapsed ballpark) at the parent commit =
   inherited. Different failure = the diff really broke something; fix the code.
b) Only then commit with --no-verify AND disclose it in the commit body: name the failing
   test, the inherited proof (parent SHA + worktree + observed result), which guard lanes
   were clean (secrets/lint), and which gates you ran by hand instead
   (ruff check, ruff format --check, the new test, and either the CI-exact suite or the
   tier-2 judge's own full-suite run).
c) Keep the bypass per-commit, never a repo-wide hook disable, and never for a gate whose
   refusal is about the diff itself.

VERIFICATION THAT THIS IS THE HONEST PATH
After the disclosed --no-verify commit, run the gitreins tier-2 judge. It executed the
repository test command independently and reported "1422 passed, 1 skipped" on the same
tree, which proves the guard's single failing id was environmental/inherited and that the
diff is green.

PITFALLS
- The guard's safety-trigger decision is not visible in the diff; read the guard header
  line ("test mode: diff, full suite — safety trigger") before assuming diff-scope.
- A live-service integration test can also flake transiently; re-run the single id once
  before building the inheritance proof, so a transient flake does not get laundered into
  a documented baseline.
- Do not silence the test with a skip marker as the "fix" unless the project's own docs
  sanction it; that converts an inherited failure into permanent lost coverage.
- --no-verify skips prepare-commit-msg hooks. If the repo relies on such a hook to append
  the required Co-authored-by trailer, append it manually to the message file, or the
  commit lands without the mandated trailer.
signatures.environment: Python 3.11 venv, gitreins Tier 1 commit guard, live docker-compose stack (FastAPI api + consensus sidecar shim), Linux host
